source_text: Καὶ ἐξῆλθον οἱ υἱοὶ Βενιαμίν. Τίνος ἕνεκεν ἡττῶνται δικαίως ἐπελθόντες; Ἥ δῆλον ὅτι διὰ προλαβούσης αἰτίας. Καὶ ὁ ψαλμός φησιν· « Ὅταν λάβω καιρὸν, ἐγὼ εὐθύτητας κρινῶ. » Εἶτα καὶ μετὰ τὸ ἡττηθῆναι, καὶ μίαν καὶ δευτέραν, μετῆλθεν ὀργὴ ἐπὶ τοὺς ἠδικηκότας, καὶ νικῶσι δίκαιαν νίκην.
thought_title: Why the Benjamites were justly defeated before their victory
orientation: Origen is closing his selections on Judges by explaining the Benjamites' initial defeats as just punishment for a prior cause, with victory coming only after wrath fell on the wrongdoers.
pass_a_gloss: And the sons of Benjamin went out. For what reason are they defeated, having come upon them justly? Or is it clear that it is because of a preceding cause? And the psalm says: "When I take the time, I will judge uprightnesses." Then also after being defeated, both once and a second time, wrath came upon those who had done wrong, and they win a just victory.

choices.english: are they defeated, having come upon them justly
choices.why: Keeps the participle's temporal/causal force and the adverb's link to the action of coming upon them, preserving the paradox Origen poses.
rejected: are they justly defeated when they attacked
are they defeated justly in their attack

choices.why: Literal rendering of the prepositional phrase; 'preceding' keeps the temporal sense of προλαβούσης, which is central to Origen's argument about prior guilt.
Preserves the plural abstract noun as in the Greek, matching the psalm wording literally rather than smoothing it.

choices.english: wrath came upon those who had done wrong
choices.why: Uses the glossary term 'wrath' for ὀργή and keeps the perfect participle's sense of completed wrongdoing.
Keeps the cognate accusative (νικῶσι νίκην) literally, preserving the rhetorical emphasis on the victory's justice.

bible_refs.note: Ὅταν λάβω καιρὸν, ἐγὼ εὐθύτητας κρινῶ

pass_b_english: And the sons of Benjamin went out. Why are they justly defeated when they came? It is clear that it was because of a preceding cause. And the psalm says, “When I take the time, I will judge uprightnesses” (Psalm 7 LXX). Then, after they were defeated once and a second time, wrath came upon those who had done wrong, and they win a just victory.

problems.quote: Why are they defeated when they came upon them justly?
problems.why: English adds an extra object “them” and misplaces “justly”, changing the sense of why the Benjamites are defeated.
problems.fix: Why are they justly defeated when they came?

edits.old: Why are they defeated when they came upon them justly?
edits.new: Why are they justly defeated when they came?

fixed: The English added an extra object 'them' and misplaced 'justly'; the source has δικαίως modifying the defeat, not the coming, so the edit restores the correct sense.

problems.source_quote: Καὶ ὁ ψαλμός φησιν· « Ὅταν λάβω καιρὸν, ἐγὼ εὐθύτητας κρινῶ. »
problems.why: The brief indicates the psalm is Psalm 7; the English cites Psalms 74/75, which is incorrect.

fixed: The psalm citation was incorrect; the source quotes Psalm 7, not Psalms 74/75, so I corrected it to (Psalm 7 LXX).
